identity.name: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Limited
identity.industry: NBFC — Diversified Retail Lending (Vehicle Finance + MSME Mortgage + Consumer/Unsecured)

summary.oneLiner: Cholamandalam Investment & Finance powers India's economic participation through disciplined vehicle finance, secured lending, and a deeply integrated CSR blueprint focused on the transport ecosystem and rural communities.
summary.business: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Limited (Chola) is a diversified NBFC serving primarily the commercial vehicle and transport ecosystem, alongside small and medium enterprises, homeowners, and consumers. It provides vehicle finance, loan against property, home loans, SME loans, consumer and small enterprise loans, and secured business and personal loans, underpinned by prudent underwriting and a diversified funding base.

currentContext.strengths: Deep, decades-long franchise in commercial vehicle financing, anchored by the 'Aarthik Engine' ecosystem and highway-centric health outreach (Project Raahi) that embeds the company with truck drivers.|Diversified, granular secured and unsecured lending portfolio with disciplined underwriting and a management overlay of ₹200 crores against geo-political risks.|Robust liquidity position with ₹21,186 crores in total liquidity (including undrawn lines) and no negative cumulative ALM mismatches across all time buckets.|Strong governance framework aligned with RBI Master Directions for Upper Layer NBFCs, with an experienced Board spanning banking, risk, compliance, and technology.
currentContext.strategies: Grow sustainably with discipline, protect asset quality, and strengthen customer relationships.|Deepen presence in smaller towns, semi-urban, and rural markets across chosen segments.|Invest in technology and AI-led interventions (collections, sales, credit) to improve turnaround times, controls, productivity, and customer experience.|Scale newer businesses responsibly — Gold Loans, SME, Secured Business & Personal Loans — around existing branch catchments.|Maintain robust governance, risk management, and cyber resilience as the business becomes more digital.|The Company has a Dividend Distribution Policy in compliance with SEBI Listing Regulations, available on its website. The policy governs dividend recommendations within prescribed ceilings and in compliance with the RBI Master Directions framework. The Board recommended a final dividend of 35% (₹0.70 per share) for FY26, following an interim dividend of 65% (₹1.30 per share), resulting in a total dividend of 100% (₹2 per share) for the year, subject to shareholder approval.|P1: Ensure 0% data breaches in customer data protection (achieved 0% breach in FY 2025-26).|P2: Pursue increase of EV loan disbursements by 5% YoY (over-achieved: ₹628.75 crores disbursed in FY 2025-26 vs ₹525.46 crores in FY 2024-25).|P3: Achieve and sustain Zero accident culture through road safety awareness initiatives and digitisation solutions for learning and development.|P6: Achieve green building status for corporate office (being pursued).|P9: Maintain ISO 27001:2022 ISMS certification for digital technology services and ISO 9001:2015 for loan disbursement and risk governance.
currentContext.expansion: The Company directed capital expenditure of ₹27.02 crores (11.38% of total capex) in FY 2025-26 towards digital and energy efficiency categories. This included investments in electric mobility, digital and software assets, energy efficient smart air conditioning, LED lighting and monitors, RFID enabled devices, safety signage, and UPS infrastructure. These initiatives support digital transformation, automation-led governance, and operational efficiency for lending operations while reducing energy consumption and emissions, improving operational reliability and strengthening long-term environmental and sustainability performance.
currentContext.mdna: India's growth story: rising aspirations, infrastructure development, formalization, digital adoption, and expanding credit access will continue to drive demand for financial services.|Vehicle Finance demand conditions strengthened towards the latter part of FY26; early delinquencies and non-starter trends improved.|Loan Against Property supported by branch expansion, healthy demand, and focused execution.|Home Loans expanding from a largely South-focused presence to a pan-India footprint, with newer branches contributing meaningfully.|Consumer & Small Enterprise Loans: tighter underwriting, improved segmentation, and sharper risk filters helped reduce credit costs and improve book quality.

risks.risk: Unsecured portfolio recalibration and asset quality
risks.note: Regulatory interventions and moderation in unsecured lending have required recalibration; while newer cohorts show improving performance, the segment remains a structural risk to portfolio resilience and growth momentum.
The Company holds a management overlay of â¹200 crores specifically for potential adverse impact of geo-political risks on its loan portfolio, indicating exposure to external shocks.
With increasing processing of sensitive data and advanced cyber threats, the Company faces risk of direct financial loss, regulatory fines, data loss, litigation, and revenue/reputation loss.
Climate change poses implications for the business, requiring transition to a carbon-neutral model; managed through BCP/DR activities and macro-economic monitoring.
The outlook notes that growth is normalising after a strong base, which could pressure disbursement growth rates and portfolio expansion across segments.

one-line thesis: Chola delivered its full-year credit-cost target in the seasonally worst quarter — net credit cost 1.5% vs 1.8% LY,
against a stated FY27 goal of 1.5% — while compounding at 23% AUM / 22% disbursements, lifting pre-tax ROTA to 3.7%
(from 3.1%) and ROE to 21.2%. The one genuine subtlety is accounting, not credit: Chola moved disbursement recognition
from cheque-handover to bank-debit date this quarter, which depresses the reported disbursement line in LAP / home loans /
SBPL / used vehicles (like-for-like ~20%+) and simultaneously flatters yields, because non-interest-earning disbursed
assets stop sitting in the AUM denominator. Management refused to raise guidance on the back of one quarter, holding
22% disbursements / 23% AUM / 1.5% credit cost / 3.5% minimum pre-tax ROTA / 8.2% NIM — every one of which Q1 already beat.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > One-offs / distortions to call out:
> 1. Disbursement-recognition change (one-time). Recognition moved from cheque-handover date to the date the cheque
>    is debited in the bank account ("provable validatable data"). Hits LAP, Home Loans, SBPL and used vehicles
>    (registration/hypothecation lag); does not hit new-vehicle finance (dealer trade advance + delivery order).
>    Like-for-like HL and LAP disbursement growth was ~20%. Mgmt: this is a Chola call for prudence, not an RBI mandate —
>    though it descends from the RBI requirement to reverse interest for the cheque-cutting-to-honour gap.
>    From Q2 FY27 the base is clean and the optical gap disappears.
> 2. Yields are marginally flattered by the same change — CFO conceded: "you will see some flip on the yields because
>    the denominator is marginally coming down." Part of the 42 bps NIM gain is definitional. Unquantified on the call.
> 3. PCR moderated sequentially for a mechanical reason — VF wrote off some 100%-provided cases; removing 100%-provided
>    GNPA against an ~48% average provisioning rate drags reported PCR down. No buffer release: the INR200 cr overlay is intact.
> 4. 3.7% is PBT-ROTA (pre-tax), not the post-tax ROA convention most NBFC peers report. Do not compare like-for-like.
> 5. PD/LGD are refreshed once a year in the December quarter (moved from March last year) — so no model-driven
>    provision movement should be expected in Q1/Q2.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Disbursement growth: 22% for FY27 — "we can still deliver 22% disbursement growth even in quarter 3 and quarter 4",
conditional on the market holding. Q2 "will definitely be better or as good as what we have done"; H2 faces a high base
(last year's growth started in H2).
AUM growth: 23% for FY27 — "23% we have already achieved, I think it is doable. We'll definitely be not going down."
Net credit cost: 1.5% for FY27, already delivered in Q1; "by end of this financial year, it will only improve."
Improvement to come from VF and CSEL, not CSEL alone. Guidance number not formally reset lower.
LAP credit cost: 0.3% (30 bps) annualised for FY27 (Q1 ran 37 bps).
SBPL credit cost: ~2.5% steady-state range (Q1 at 2.3%) — designed high-yield/high-loss economics.
PBT-ROTA: 3.5% minimum, explicitly framed as a floor, not a forecast — "we will try to hold it or try to improve it."
Declined to put a number on Q4 FY27 exit ROTA.
NIM: hold 8.2% ("we are hoping that we hold it"). CFO: cost of funds flat → "NIM will improve", but "let's not
count the chicken before."
Cost of funds: up ~10 bps near-term; flat for the full year vs FY26 as a % of average assets — assuming a
25–50 bps repo hike. Shape inverts vs last year: H1 low / H2 high this year (LY was H1 high / H2 low).
The 30 bps of CoF benefit enjoyed so far "cannot be there for full year."
Gold loans: AUM to INR5,000 cr this financial year (from INR2,143 cr); 360 new branches; new branches to reach
INR12–15 cr AUM per branch within FY27 and be profitable by next year-end; steady-state PBT-ROTA >4% after 3 years,
targeted "on par" with listed gold-loan incumbents.
CSEL: ROA to move from 3.3% to 3.6–3.7% and then above the company ROA; NCL already cut from 6.7% to 4.7%.
Branch expansion: 125 VF resident locations converted to full-fledged branches by end of FY27; affordable housing
and LAP each opening 100+ branches; home-loan branch expansion "going to take over in next 6 months' time."
Capital: remaining INR430 cr of CCDs to convert in October 2026 (INR1,370 cr converted in FY26 + INR200 cr in Jul-2026,
of the INR2,000 cr issue). CFO deflated its importance: "It's not a game changer."
Buffer provision: INR200 cr overlay held; view to be taken at the end of FY27.
Not guided: opex ratio, NII, absolute PAT, FY27 exit ROTA, any IRDAI-circular impact.
disbursement pipeline / aum growth (subs: There is no order book; the forward-visibility proxy is disbursement momentum plus the base effect. Management said demand
is intact across every product line — "vehicle finance or loan against property or housing loan or SME or SBPL or CSEL or
gold and even consumer durable" — and that July has already been better than expected. The shape of FY27 is explicit:
Q2 is de-risked ("definitely better or as good as"), while H2 carries the hard comparison because last year's growth only
began in H2. The offset management is banking on is market-share gain in the newer engines (CSEL, SME, SBPL) plus the clean
disbursement base from Q2 once the recognition change annualises out. The stated hard dependency is the market staying where
it is — "if market continues to be what it is now… we can still deliver 22%."
segment / subsidiary detail: Segment AUM shares derived from the disclosed AUMs (not stated on the call): Vehicle Finance ~49%, MSME (LAP+SME+SBPL) ~27%,
Consumer (HL+CSEL+Gold) ~16%, balance ~8% other/unallocated.
Vehicle Finance — INR1,24,132 cr AUM (+19%), disbursements +21%. New and used together grew >20% in disbursements;
the used book was optically hit by the recognition change (registration/hypothecation lag), new vehicles were not
(dealer trade advance + delivery order). Stage 3 4.05% (Jun-26) vs 3.84% (Mar-26) — a +21 bps seasonal step vs +45 bps in the
same quarter last year, which is management's core asset-quality argument. Some 100%-provided cases written off this quarter.
Distribution: 600+ resident locations, 125 converting to full branches in FY27.
Loan Against Property / home equity — INR54,130 cr AUM (+23%). Yields up 30 bps QoQ and YoY, explicitly not
from direct-assignment income (DA is reported separately, outside business P&L) but from mix shift into small-ticket LAP
and deeper-tier geographies. Loan losses 37 bps in Q1, guided to 0.3% annualised. Stage 3 held in a 2.3–2.5% band YoY;
management "pretty confident this will be resolved." Explicitly one of the four above-company-ROA businesses.
Home Loans (affordable housing) — INR23,644 cr AUM (+22%). Yield up from 15.5% (FY26) to 15.9% and pre-tax ROA
from 3.9% to 4.7% — so the analyst-flagged 60 bps QoQ yield dip is a Q4-vs-Q1 collection-income seasonality artefact,
not compression. Moving to slightly bigger ticket sizes; branch expansion just started, effect due in ~6 months.
SME — INR9,923 cr AUM (+39%). Cited as a market-share gainer; no separate P&L disclosure.
SBPL — INR3,730 cr AUM (+40%), disbursements "30% plus" ex-recognition-change. Pre-tax ROA 7.9% — far above company
level and "much higher than our expectation"; NCL 2.3%, steady state ~2.5% by design (very small merchants, deep-tier towns,
high yields). Stage 3 is lumpy by construction: small-ticket NBFC lending has no SARFAESI, so recoveries route through
an ARC and NPAs step down only in quarters when an ARC sale is executed (one done last quarter, another planned next).
CSEL — INR15,884 cr AUM (+12%). The deliberate laggard: fintech originations have been "knocked off". NCL cut 200 bps
from 6.7% to 4.7%; ROA 3.3% — versus an internal expectation of 3% only by Q3, i.e. two quarters early. Approval rates
35–40% (business loans), ~60% (salaried). FEMI (first-EMI default) steady at ~3% for 15 months, though the business head
said he tracks 6-MOB / 12-MOB vintages instead, which are improving post credit-check tightening. 55% of collections digital.
Gold Loans — INR2,143 cr AUM. Per-branch AUM already INR12–15 cr and rising. Yields "on par or slightly a shade better"
than listed peers — analyst framed 16–17%, management assented. 90% of customers are new to Chola; ~20–25% are new to
gold loans entirely. Products: bullet and EMI; largely consumption (6–12 month tenure) with income-generating loans just
launched (6–9 months). Operating model is stand-alone branches in tightly defined ~3 km micro-markets (all other
products co-habit premises).
Collections infrastructure (group-wide): ~30,000 people, three-tier (soft / hard / recovery), product-specific models.
growth verticals / optionality: Gold loans as a customer-acquisition funnel, not a cross-sell play. Management explicitly is not cross-selling gold
into the existing book — analysis found only INR700–800 cr of gold borrowing across Chola's entire national customer base.
The stated optionality runs the other way: gold brings high volumes of new-to-Chola customers who can later be sold
Chola's other products (Vellayan: "the reverse opportunity… cross-selling into them also over time can be good").
Income-generating gold loans just launched — a higher-quality, business-purpose extension of a consumption book.
CSEL rebuild post-fintech — the book is being regrown on own-underwritten originations with tightened credit checks;
ROA already 3.3% and heading above company level, which converts a former problem child into an ROA accretor.
Small-ticket LAP / deep-tier penetration — the source of the LAP yield expansion and, per management, unthreatened by
the Mudra ceiling increase (see §10).
Four designated above-company-ROA engines: LAP, affordable housing, SBPL and CSEL — "all 4 businesses are meant for
delivering more than the company ROA."
6a. moat & competitive position: Priority-sector-lending bargaining power on bank funding. CFO, asked directly whether banks now have more pricing power
over NBFCs: "we borrow mostly the priority sector loans. So, there we have a better bargaining power over them."
Concretely, Chola pays no premium over MCLR — "We take it at MCLR" — and on the short (1–3 month) MCLR at that.
Bank loans are ~50% of borrowings, of which only 25–30% is MCLR-linked.
Distribution depth as the acquisition asset. 600+ VF resident locations plus 100+ branch additions each in affordable
housing and LAP; management attributes the SME/CSEL/SBPL share gains to reach in under-penetrated markets rather than price.
Brand as the gold-loan right-to-win. Explicitly evidenced rather than asserted: gold is a trust business in a 3 km
micro-market, and Chola is "riding on the trust that customers have on Chola as a brand", combined with fully digital
branch journeys — which is why 90% new-to-Chola acquisition is working without price leadership.
ALM discipline. CFO rebutted the FY26 annual-report ALM mismatch read: the AR column is a regulator-defined format,
not the full ALM; on a cumulative basis "there is no negative cumulative mismatch in any of the buckets, and that's
been our trend right throughout."
margins & cost dynamics: NIM at 8.2%, up 42 bps YoY, driven by lower cost of funds — with a definitional tailwind from the disbursement-recognition
change shrinking the AUM denominator. The forward margin question is entirely a liability question and management framed it
as a shape call, not a level call: last year H1 was expensive and H2 cheap; this year inverts. Bank funding is holding
(PSL bargaining power, borrowed at MCLR with no spread), but market/bond funding "has been slightly hardening" and the CFO
is openly "worried whether the second half there will be a rate increase." Working assumption: repo +25–50 bps, CoF +~10 bps,
full-year CoF flat as a % of average assets. Bank borrowing is currently cheaper than bonds, but MCLR-linked exposure re-prices
upward on a repo hike while bonds are fixed — so the mix decision is a visibility-vs-cost trade. On the asset side, mix is
moving favourably (CSEL regrowing, gold scaling, small-ticket LAP deepening). Management therefore says NIM should improve but
declined to bank it. Opex was not discussed at all on this call — a genuine disclosure gap this quarter.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Not a capex business; expansion is branch and headcount.
Gold loans: 360 new stand-alone branches this year, each targeted at INR12–15 cr AUM within FY27 and profitable by
next year-end. This is the single largest checkable physical commitment on the call.
Vehicle finance: 125 resident locations → full-fledged branches by end of FY27, from a 600+ resident-location base;
conversion is threshold-driven on disbursement volume.
Affordable housing and LAP: 100+ branch additions each, described as the normal annual run-rate.
Home loans: branch expansion started this quarter, revenue effect expected over "next 6 months."
capital allocation: CAR 19.81% with Tier 1 at 14.81% as of June 2026 — described as "ample headroom to support future growth"; no equity raise
discussed. The INR2,000 cr CCD programme is nearly done: INR1,370 cr converted in FY26, INR200 cr in July 2026, INR430 cr
due October 2026. Management deliberately talked down its significance — against ~INR2,20,000 cr of borrowings the CFO
called it "very small… not a game changer" — a useful correction to the sell-side narrative that CCD conversion would drive
FY27 margin. The INR200 cr management overlay is being held rather than released to flatter credit cost, with a decision
deferred to FY27-end. Liquidity carried at INR23,984 cr including undrawn lines. No dividend or buyback commentary.
risks & watch-items: Below-average monsoon / El Nino — IMD prediction cited at 92% of normal vs 96% average. Management's position is
conditional, not dismissive: "If that happens, then it will not be so bad", with no visibility into Q3 while the rains
are unfinished. The standing NBFC view (repeated to Chola by peers) is that a weak monsoon hits next year, not this one.
H2 base effect — the explicit soft spot in the 22% disbursement guidance; last year's growth came entirely in H2.
Repo hike in H2 — a 25–50 bps hike is already assumed in the flat-CoF guidance. A larger move breaks H2 NIM;
MCLR-linked bank borrowing re-prices while bonds do not.
IRDAI circular on insurance — flagged unprompted by the CFO as an unquantified overhang on (presumably) insurance-linked
fee income; he twice refused to size it — "Let the circular come, we'll decide about it. It's not going to happen for this
financial year is what I hear." Watch for the circular and for the associated opex, which he also declined to disclose.
West Asia crisis / tariffs — named as macro uncertainties constraining management's forecast horizon to "1 or 2 quarters".
SBPL Stage 3 optics — will keep sawtoothing with ARC-sale timing because small-ticket NBFC lending has no SARFAESI recourse.
Mudra ceiling raised to INR20 lakh unsecured — a potential substitute for small-ticket LAP / home equity.
Chola's read: logins have actually improved, because these borrowers want fast turnaround plus long-tenure repayment,
"we are not seeing any trend as of now on this segment." Worth re-checking in two quarters.
PCR trending down — mechanically explained this quarter, but a repeat without write-off backing would be a real signal.
Guidance is not being raised despite a beat — if 1.5% credit cost holds through a seasonal Q2/Q3, the risk is that
the un-reset guidance keeps expectations anchored low rather than that the number slips.
management quality / tone: Assertive to the point of combative on asset quality — Kundu opened his first answer by rejecting the premise
("I don't know why you're saying it has gone up"), then made analysts do the arithmetic his way: compare Stage 2 + Stage 3
together and compare Q4→Q1 deltas against the prior year's Q4→Q1 delta, not levels. On that frame the argument holds
(+25 bps vs +45 bps in VF; total delinquency −20 bps YoY), and he invited direct comparison against any other NBFC's
delinquency stack. Notably un-promotional where it would have been easy to promote: the CFO killed the CCD-conversion
margin narrative, refused to size the IRDAI risk without the circular in hand, and warned that the 30 bps CoF benefit
"cannot be there for full year"; Kundu refused to name a Q4 exit ROTA and explained why conservatism is warranted
("all 3-line items don't support" simultaneously). Business heads were pushed forward to answer their own numbers
(LAP, CSEL, gold, VF branches) with specifics rather than deflection — a good disclosure signal. The one soft spot is
disclosure breadth: no opex, NII or absolute PAT discussion at all, and the gold-loan ROTA target was extracted by an
analyst rather than volunteered.
non-obvious takeaways: The accounting change cuts both ways, and only one side was scrutinised. Analysts spent four separate exchanges on how
the recognition change depressed disbursements. Almost nobody pushed on the CFO's own admission that it raises reported
yields — assets that previously sat in AUM earning nothing (interest was being manually reversed to comply with RBI's
cheque-gap rule) are no longer in the denominator. So an unquantified slice of the 42 bps NIM gain is definitional. The
clean read on FY27 margin only arrives with Q2, on a like-for-like base.
3.7% is pre-tax ROTA, not post-tax ROA. Cross-NBFC screens that stack Chola's 3.7% against peers' post-tax 2–2.5%
overstate the gap by roughly the tax rate. Management's own floor is stated as "3.5% pretax."
Hitting the full-year credit-cost target in the seasonally worst quarter turns 1.5% into a ceiling, not a target.
Kundu said as much ("by end of this financial year, it will only improve") but did not reset the guidance number —
leaving an un-priced option that Q2/Q3 can exercise. This is the cleanest checkable asymmetry on the call.
The ROA story is a mix story, not a credit story. Four businesses — LAP, affordable housing, SBPL (7.9% pre-tax ROA)
and CSEL (3.3% and rising) — are all designed to earn above company ROA. Arithmetically that makes Vehicle Finance,
still ~49% of AUM, the dilutive core. Company ROA therefore rises as VF's share falls, independent of credit performance.
Gold loans are an acquisition channel disguised as a product. With only INR700–800 cr of gold borrowing found across
Chola's entire existing customer base and 90% of gold customers new to Chola, the internal cross-sell thesis is dead —
the value is the reverse funnel into a book that has never touched these customers. That reframes 360 branches from
"me-too gold expansion" to distribution capex for a new customer pool.
The CFO disclosed the borrowing base by accident. Deflating the CCD question produced "~INR2,20,000 crores borrowing" —
a number not otherwise given on the call, and the denominator needed to check the flat-CoF claim next quarter.
SBPL's NPA line is a calendar, not a credit signal. No SARFAESI for small-ticket NBFC lending means Stage 3 steps down
only in quarters with an ARC transaction. Reading the sequential move as credit deterioration/improvement is a category error.
CoF guidance is a bet on a specific rate path. "Flat for the full year" is conditioned on a 25–50 bps repo hike arriving.
No hike would be upside to NIM; a larger hike breaks it — and Chola's short-dated (1–3 month) MCLR borrowing re-prices fast.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1 FY27 (this): First note for CHOLAFIN in this universe. Disbursements INR29,612 cr (+22%), AUM INR2,54,392 cr (+23%);
SBPL INR3,730 cr (+40%), Gold INR2,143 cr. NIM 8.2% (+42 bps), net credit cost 1.5% (from 1.8% — FY27 target hit in Q1),
Stage 3 3.29% (+13 bps YoY, +25 bps QoQ vs +45 bps LY), Stage 2 −33 bps, total delinquency ~6% (−20 bps). PBT-ROTA 3.7% (from 3.1%),
ROE 21.2%. CAR 19.81% / Tier 1 14.81%. INR200 cr overlay intact. Disbursement recognition changed to bank-debit date
(one-time; LAP/HL/SBPL/used-vehicle affected; like-for-like ~20%+). FY27 guidance set: 22% disbursements, 23% AUM,
1.5% credit cost, 3.5% minimum pre-tax ROTA, 8.2% NIM held, CoF flat on a 25–50 bps repo-hike assumption,
gold AUM INR5,000 cr + 360 branches, 125 VF resident locations → branches, INR430 cr CCD conversion due Oct-2026.
Q2 FY27 → check: (1) disbursement growth on the clean base — does 22% survive without the recognition drag, and does the
yield/NIM gain persist once the denominator effect annualises; (2) is net credit cost below 1.5% as promised, and is the
1.5% guidance formally reset; (3) VF Stage 3 reversing off 4.05% into the seasonal improvement window; (4) LAP loan loss
tracking to 0.3% annualised (Q1 ran 37 bps); (5) CoF trajectory vs the flat-FY claim and whether the assumed 25–50 bps repo
hike materialised — measure against the ~INR2,20,000 cr borrowing base; (6) gold AUM run-rate toward INR5,000 cr and branch
count added against 360; (7) CSEL ROA toward 3.6–3.7% and NCL below 4.7%; (8) SBPL Stage 3 step-down on the planned ARC sale;
(9) INR430 cr CCD conversion executed in October; (10) INR200 cr overlay still unconsumed; (11) IRDAI circular published/sized;
(12) monsoon outturn vs the 92% forecast and any Q3 commentary shift.

> 5. PD/LGD are refreshed once a year in the December quarter (moved from March last year) — so no model-driven
>    provision movement should be expected in Q1/Q2.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Disbursement growth: 22% for FY27 — "we can still deliver 22% disbursement growth even in quarter 3 and quarter 4",
conditional on the market holding. Q2 "will definitely be better or as good as what we have done"; H2 faces a high base
(last year's growth started in H2).
AUM growth: 23% for FY27 — "23% we have already achieved, I think it is doable. We'll definitely be not going down."
Net credit cost: 1.5% for FY27, already delivered in Q1; "by end of this financial year, it will only improve."
Improvement to come from VF and CSEL, not CSEL alone. Guidance number not formally reset lower.
LAP credit cost: 0.3% (30 bps) annualised for FY27 (Q1 ran 37 bps).
SBPL credit cost: ~2.5% steady-state range (Q1 at 2.3%) — designed high-yield/high-loss economics.
PBT-ROTA: 3.5% minimum, explicitly framed as a floor, not a forecast — "we will try to hold it or try to improve it."
Declined to put a number on Q4 FY27 exit ROTA.
NIM: hold 8.2% ("we are hoping that we hold it"). CFO: cost of funds flat → "NIM will improve", but "let's not
count the chicken before."
Cost of funds: up ~10 bps near-term; flat for the full year vs FY26 as a % of average assets — assuming a
25–50 bps repo hike. Shape inverts vs last year: H1 low / H2 high this year (LY was H1 high / H2 low).
The 30 bps of CoF benefit enjoyed so far "cannot be there for full year."
Gold loans: AUM to INR5,000 cr this financial year (from INR2,143 cr); 360 new branches; new branches to reach
INR12–15 cr AUM per branch within FY27 and be profitable by next year-end; steady-state PBT-ROTA >4% after 3 years,
targeted "on par" with listed gold-loan incumbents.
CSEL: ROA to move from 3.3% to 3.6–3.7% and then above the company ROA; NCL already cut from 6.7% to 4.7%.
Branch expansion: 125 VF resident locations converted to full-fledged branches by end of FY27; affordable housing
and LAP each opening 100+ branches; home-loan branch expansion "going to take over in next 6 months' time."
Capital: remaining INR430 cr of CCDs to convert in October 2026 (INR1,370 cr converted in FY26 + INR200 cr in Jul-2026,
of the INR2,000 cr issue). CFO deflated its importance: "It's not a game changer."
Buffer provision: INR200 cr overlay held; view to be taken at the end of FY27.
Not guided: opex ratio, NII, absolute PAT, FY27 exit ROTA, any IRDAI-circular impact.
disbursement pipeline / aum growth (subs: There is no order book; the forward-visibility proxy is disbursement momentum plus the base effect. Management said demand
is intact across every product line — "vehicle finance or loan against property or housing loan or SME or SBPL or CSEL or
gold and even consumer durable" — and that July has already been better than expected. The shape of FY27 is explicit:
Q2 is de-risked ("definitely better or as good as"), while H2 carries the hard comparison because last year's growth only
began in H2. The offset management is banking on is market-share gain in the newer engines (CSEL, SME, SBPL) plus the clean
disbursement base from Q2 once the recognition change annualises out. The stated hard dependency is the market staying where
it is — "if market continues to be what it is now… we can still deliver 22%."
segment / subsidiary detail: Segment AUM shares derived from the disclosed AUMs (not stated on the call): Vehicle Finance ~49%, MSME (LAP+SME+SBPL) ~27%,
Consumer (HL+CSEL+Gold) ~16%, balance ~8% other/unallocated.
Vehicle Finance — INR1,24,132 cr AUM (+19%), disbursements +21%. New and used together grew >20% in disbursements;
the used book was optically hit by the recognition change (registration/hypothecation lag), new vehicles were not
(dealer trade advance + delivery order). Stage 3 4.05% (Jun-26) vs 3.84% (Mar-26) — a +21 bps seasonal step vs +45 bps in the
same quarter last year, which is management's core asset-quality argument. Some 100%-provided cases written off this quarter.
Distribution: 600+ resident locations, 125 converting to full branches in FY27.
Loan Against Property / home equity — INR54,130 cr AUM (+23%). Yields up 30 bps QoQ and YoY, explicitly not
from direct-assignment income (DA is reported separately, outside business P&L) but from mix shift into small-ticket LAP
and deeper-tier geographies. Loan losses 37 bps in Q1, guided to 0.3% annualised. Stage 3 held in a 2.3–2.5% band YoY;
management "pretty confident this will be resolved." Explicitly one of the four above-company-ROA businesses.
Home Loans (affordable housing) — INR23,644 cr AUM (+22%). Yield up from 15.5% (FY26) to 15.9% and pre-tax ROA
from 3.9% to 4.7% — so the analyst-flagged 60 bps QoQ yield dip is a Q4-vs-Q1 collection-income seasonality artefact,
not compression. Moving to slightly bigger ticket sizes; branch expansion just started, effect due in ~6 months.
SME — INR9,923 cr AUM (+39%). Cited as a market-share gainer; no separate P&L disclosure.
SBPL — INR3,730 cr AUM (+40%), disbursements "30% plus" ex-recognition-change. Pre-tax ROA 7.9% — far above company
level and "much higher than our expectation"; NCL 2.3%, steady state ~2.5% by design (very small merchants, deep-tier towns,
high yields). Stage 3 is lumpy by construction: small-ticket NBFC lending has no SARFAESI, so recoveries route through
an ARC and NPAs step down only in quarters when an ARC sale is executed (one done last quarter, another planned next).
CSEL — INR15,884 cr AUM (+12%). The deliberate laggard: fintech originations have been "knocked off". NCL cut 200 bps
from 6.7% to 4.7%; ROA 3.3% — versus an internal expectation of 3% only by Q3, i.e. two quarters early. Approval rates
35–40% (business loans), ~60% (salaried). FEMI (first-EMI default) steady at ~3% for 15 months, though the business head
said he tracks 6-MOB / 12-MOB vintages instead, which are improving post credit-check tightening. 55% of collections digital.
Gold Loans — INR2,143 cr AUM. Per-branch AUM already INR12–15 cr and rising. Yields "on par or slightly a shade better"
than listed peers — analyst framed 16–17%, management assented. 90% of customers are new to Chola; ~20–25% are new to
gold loans entirely. Products: bullet and EMI; largely consumption (6–12 month tenure) with income-generating loans just
launched (6–9 months). Operating model is stand-alone branches in tightly defined ~3 km micro-markets (all other
products co-habit premises).
Collections infrastructure (group-wide): ~30,000 people, three-tier (soft / hard / recovery), product-specific models.
growth verticals / optionality: Gold loans as a customer-acquisition funnel, not a cross-sell play. Management explicitly is not cross-selling gold
into the existing book — analysis found only INR700–800 cr of gold borrowing across Chola's entire national customer base.
The stated optionality runs the other way: gold brings high volumes of new-to-Chola customers who can later be sold
Chola's other products (Vellayan: "the reverse opportunity… cross-selling into them also over time can be good").
Income-generating gold loans just launched — a higher-quality, business-purpose extension of a consumption book.
CSEL rebuild post-fintech — the book is being regrown on own-underwritten originations with tightened credit checks;
ROA already 3.3% and heading above company level, which converts a former problem child into an ROA accretor.
Small-ticket LAP / deep-tier penetration — the source of the LAP yield expansion and, per management, unthreatened by
the Mudra ceiling increase (see §10).
Four designated above-company-ROA engines: LAP, affordable housing, SBPL and CSEL — "all 4 businesses are meant for
delivering more than the company ROA."
6a. moat & competitive position: Priority-sector-lending bargaining power on bank funding. CFO, asked directly whether banks now have more pricing power
over NBFCs: "we borrow mostly the priority sector loans. So, there we have a better bargaining power over them."
Concretely, Chola pays no premium over MCLR — "We take it at MCLR" — and on the short (1–3 month) MCLR at that.
Bank loans are ~50% of borrowings, of which only 25–30% is MCLR-linked.
Distribution depth as the acquisition asset. 600+ VF resident locations plus 100+ branch additions each in affordable
housing and LAP; management attributes the SME/CSEL/SBPL share gains to reach in under-penetrated markets rather than price.
Brand as the gold-loan right-to-win. Explicitly evidenced rather than asserted: gold is a trust business in a 3 km
micro-market, and Chola is "riding on the trust that customers have on Chola as a brand", combined with fully digital
branch journeys — which is why 90% new-to-Chola acquisition is working without price leadership.
ALM discipline. CFO rebutted the FY26 annual-report ALM mismatch read: the AR column is a regulator-defined format,
not the full ALM; on a cumulative basis "there is no negative cumulative mismatch in any of the buckets, and that's
been our trend right throughout."
margins & cost dynamics: NIM at 8.2%, up 42 bps YoY, driven by lower cost of funds — with a definitional tailwind from the disbursement-recognition
change shrinking the AUM denominator. The forward margin question is entirely a liability question and management framed it
as a shape call, not a level call: last year H1 was expensive and H2 cheap; this year inverts. Bank funding is holding
(PSL bargaining power, borrowed at MCLR with no spread), but market/bond funding "has been slightly hardening" and the CFO
is openly "worried whether the second half there will be a rate increase." Working assumption: repo +25–50 bps, CoF +~10 bps,
full-year CoF flat as a % of average assets. Bank borrowing is currently cheaper than bonds, but MCLR-linked exposure re-prices
upward on a repo hike while bonds are fixed — so the mix decision is a visibility-vs-cost trade. On the asset side, mix is
moving favourably (CSEL regrowing, gold scaling, small-ticket LAP deepening). Management therefore says NIM should improve but
declined to bank it. Opex was not discussed at all on this call — a genuine disclosure gap this quarter.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Not a capex business; expansion is branch and headcount.
Gold loans: 360 new stand-alone branches this year, each targeted at INR12–15 cr AUM within FY27 and profitable by
next year-end. This is the single largest checkable physical commitment on the call.
Vehicle finance: 125 resident locations → full-fledged branches by end of FY27, from a 600+ resident-location base;
conversion is threshold-driven on disbursement volume.
Affordable housing and LAP: 100+ branch additions each, described as the normal annual run-rate.
Home loans: branch expansion started this quarter, revenue effect expected over "next 6 months."
capital allocation: CAR 19.81% with Tier 1 at 14.81% as of June 2026 — described as "ample headroom to support future growth"; no equity raise
discussed. The INR2,000 cr CCD programme is nearly done: INR1,370 cr converted in FY26, INR200 cr in July 2026, INR430 cr
due October 2026. Management deliberately talked down its significance — against ~INR2,20,000 cr of borrowings the CFO
called it "very small… not a game changer" — a useful correction to the sell-side narrative that CCD conversion would drive
FY27 margin. The INR200 cr management overlay is being held rather than released to flatter credit cost, with a decision
deferred to FY27-end. Liquidity carried at INR23,984 cr including undrawn lines. No dividend or buyback commentary.
risks & watch-items: Below-average monsoon / El Nino — IMD prediction cited at 92% of normal vs 96% average. Management's position is
conditional, not dismissive: "If that happens, then it will not be so bad", with no visibility into Q3 while the rains
are unfinished. The standing NBFC view (repeated to Chola by peers) is that a weak monsoon hits next year, not this one.
H2 base effect — the explicit soft spot in the 22% disbursement guidance; last year's growth came entirely in H2.
Repo hike in H2 — a 25–50 bps hike is already assumed in the flat-CoF guidance. A larger move breaks H2 NIM;
MCLR-linked bank borrowing re-prices while bonds do not.
IRDAI circular on insurance — flagged unprompted by the CFO as an unquantified overhang on (presumably) insurance-linked
fee income; he twice refused to size it — "Let the circular come, we'll decide about it. It's not going to happen for this
financial year is what I hear." Watch for the circular and for the associated opex, which he also declined to disclose.
West Asia crisis / tariffs — named as macro uncertainties constraining management's forecast horizon to "1 or 2 quarters".
SBPL Stage 3 optics — will keep sawtoothing with ARC-sale timing because small-ticket NBFC lending has no SARFAESI recourse.
Mudra ceiling raised to INR20 lakh unsecured — a potential substitute for small-ticket LAP / home equity.
Chola's read: logins have actually improved, because these borrowers want fast turnaround plus long-tenure repayment,
"we are not seeing any trend as of now on this segment." Worth re-checking in two quarters.
PCR trending down — mechanically explained this quarter, but a repeat without write-off backing would be a real signal.
Guidance is not being raised despite a beat — if 1.5% credit cost holds through a seasonal Q2/Q3, the risk is that
the un-reset guidance keeps expectations anchored low rather than that the number slips.
management quality / tone: Assertive to the point of combative on asset quality — Kundu opened his first answer by rejecting the premise
("I don't know why you're saying it has gone up"), then made analysts do the arithmetic his way: compare Stage 2 + Stage 3
together and compare Q4→Q1 deltas against the prior year's Q4→Q1 delta, not levels. On that frame the argument holds
(+25 bps vs +45 bps in VF; total delinquency −20 bps YoY), and he invited direct comparison against any other NBFC's
delinquency stack. Notably un-promotional where it would have been easy to promote: the CFO killed the CCD-conversion
margin narrative, refused to size the IRDAI risk without the circular in hand, and warned that the 30 bps CoF benefit
"cannot be there for full year"; Kundu refused to name a Q4 exit ROTA and explained why conservatism is warranted
("all 3-line items don't support" simultaneously). Business heads were pushed forward to answer their own numbers
(LAP, CSEL, gold, VF branches) with specifics rather than deflection — a good disclosure signal. The one soft spot is
disclosure breadth: no opex, NII or absolute PAT discussion at all, and the gold-loan ROTA target was extracted by an
analyst rather than volunteered.
non-obvious takeaways: The accounting change cuts both ways, and only one side was scrutinised. Analysts spent four separate exchanges on how
the recognition change depressed disbursements. Almost nobody pushed on the CFO's own admission that it raises reported
yields — assets that previously sat in AUM earning nothing (interest was being manually reversed to comply with RBI's
cheque-gap rule) are no longer in the denominator. So an unquantified slice of the 42 bps NIM gain is definitional. The
clean read on FY27 margin only arrives with Q2, on a like-for-like base.
3.7% is pre-tax ROTA, not post-tax ROA. Cross-NBFC screens that stack Chola's 3.7% against peers' post-tax 2–2.5%
overstate the gap by roughly the tax rate. Management's own floor is stated as "3.5% pretax."
Hitting the full-year credit-cost target in the seasonally worst quarter turns 1.5% into a ceiling, not a target.
Kundu said as much ("by end of this financial year, it will only improve") but did not reset the guidance number —
leaving an un-priced option that Q2/Q3 can exercise. This is the cleanest checkable asymmetry on the call.
The ROA story is a mix story, not a credit story. Four businesses — LAP, affordable housing, SBPL (7.9% pre-tax ROA)
and CSEL (3.3% and rising) — are all designed to earn above company ROA. Arithmetically that makes Vehicle Finance,
still ~49% of AUM, the dilutive core. Company ROA therefore rises as VF's share falls, independent of credit performance.
Gold loans are an acquisition channel disguised as a product. With only INR700–800 cr of gold borrowing found across
Chola's entire existing customer base and 90% of gold customers new to Chola, the internal cross-sell thesis is dead —
the value is the reverse funnel into a book that has never touched these customers. That reframes 360 branches from
"me-too gold expansion" to distribution capex for a new customer pool.
The CFO disclosed the borrowing base by accident. Deflating the CCD question produced "~INR2,20,000 crores borrowing" —
a number not otherwise given on the call, and the denominator needed to check the flat-CoF claim next quarter.
SBPL's NPA line is a calendar, not a credit signal. No SARFAESI for small-ticket NBFC lending means Stage 3 steps down
only in quarters with an ARC transaction. Reading the sequential move as credit deterioration/improvement is a category error.
CoF guidance is a bet on a specific rate path. "Flat for the full year" is conditioned on a 25–50 bps repo hike arriving.
No hike would be upside to NIM; a larger hike breaks it — and Chola's short-dated (1–3 month) MCLR borrowing re-prices fast.
